hints: Notice the contact conditions: the ground is icy and frictionless but the wall is rough, so only one contact can provide friction.
Recall that $W$ always acts vertically down at the centre, and a frictionless surface can only push perpendicular to the surface.
Connect the sliding motion to friction at the wall: the top of the ladder slides down, so wall friction acts up and combines with the horizontal push from the wall to tilt $P$.
walkthrough: Identify the three forces on the ladder: $W$ is the weight of the ladder acting at its centre, $R$ is the contact force from the ground at the foot, and $P$ is the contact force from the wall at the top.

State the rule for $W$ and $R$: weight always acts vertically down, and because the ground is frictionless it can only exert a normal force perpendicular to the horizontal ground, so $R$ must be vertical.
State the rule for $P$: the wall is rough, so it exerts a horizontal normal force pushing the ladder away from the wall plus a friction force parallel to the wall.
Determine the direction of wall friction: as the ladder slides the top moves down the wall, so kinetic friction opposes this motion and acts up the wall.
Combine the wall forces: horizontal push to the right plus upward friction gives a resultant $P$ angled upward from the horizontal, while $W$ is down and $R$ is up.

options.A: R vertical and W vertical are correct, but P horizontal shows only the normal force from the wall and omits the upward friction from the rough wall.
options.B: W acts vertically down, R is vertical because icy ground has no friction, and P is tilted up from the horizontal because the rough wall provides a horizontal normal force plus vertical friction.
options.C: R tilted away from the vertical would require friction at the ground, but the ground is stated to be frictionless so R must be vertical.
options.D: P tilted upwards correctly includes wall friction, but R tilted away from the vertical is impossible on frictionless ground.
